title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
summary: Given a string of block colors 'W' (white) and 'B' (black), and an integer k, find the least number of operations to make at least one sequence of k consecutive 'B' blocks.
statement: Given a string of block colors 'W' (white) and 'B' (black), and an integer k, find the least number of operations to make at least one sequence of k consecutive 'B' blocks. An operation consists of changing a 'W' to a 'B'.
constraints: Each character is B for black or W for white.
Recoloring one white block black costs one operation.
Return the minimum recolors needed to create some contiguous run of k black blocks.
hints: For a fixed length-k window, its number of white blocks is exactly its recolor cost.
Count white blocks in the first window.
Slide one position at a time, adding the entering white indicator and subtracting the leaving one; keep the minimum.
Every possible target run is one length-k window, so the minimum window cost is optimal.
editorial: Every possible target run is one length-k window, so the minimum window cost is optimal.

tests.explanation: The best length-seven window contains three white blocks, so three recolors suffice.
A pair of adjacent black blocks already exists, so zero recolors are needed.
